part.text:
Let me set up a Maven Java project. The standard logging facade is SLF4J. I'll use slf4j-api for the facade and logback-classic as the runtime implementation (or slf4j-simple). Standard best practice: slf4j-api in compile scope, runtime implementation. Let me create the project structure.

Let me create:
- pom.xml
- src/main/java/com/example/App.java
- src/main/resources/logback.xml (if logback)
- src/test/java/...

Let me decide groupId/artifactId. I'll use com.example, app. Let me use slf4j 2.0.16 and logback 1.5.x. Java 26 available, but target a reasonable version - use 21 LTS perhaps. Let me set maven.compiler.release to 21.

Let me create the files.
A standard logging facade is SLF4J. I'll scaffold the project with `slf4j-api` as the compile-time facade and Logback as the runtime binding.

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>app</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>app</name>
    <description>Maven Java project using SLF4J as the logging facade</description>

    <properties>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <maven.compiler.release>21</maven.compiler.release>

        <slf4j.version>2.0.16</slf4j.version>
        <logback.version>1.5.16</logback.version>
        <junit.version>5.11.4</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- Logging facade: application code compiles against this only -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
            <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
            <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Runtime binding: swap this out to change the logging backend -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>ch.qos.logback</groupId>
            <artifactId>logback-classic</artifactId>
            <version>${logback.version}</version>
            <scope>runtime</scope>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.13.0</version>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.2</version>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.4.2</version>
                <configuration>
                    <archive>
                        <manifest>
                            <mainClass>com.example.App</mainClass>
                        </manifest>
                    </archive>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

The project scaffold is fine, but for demonstrating a runnable app, let me add the exec-maven-plugin or assembly. The user's core need is the project setup; a runnable jar is a nice-to-have. But maybe simpler to not over-engineer. Still, an executable jar with a facade dependency is broken unless shaded. Let me add the shade plugin so `java -jar` works.

Let me add maven-shade-plugin to produce a runnable uber jar. But shade plugin creates `original-` jar replacement. With logback-classic runtime scope, shade includes runtime deps. Good.

Actually the user's request was just "set up a new Maven Java project that needs a standard logging facade". The essential deliverable is pom + source using SLF4J. Let me make it actually runnable though, it's a good verification. I'll add shade plugin.
The plain jar has no bundled classes. I'll add the shade plugin so `java -jar` works with the facade + binding.

input.newString:
<plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.4.2</version>
                <configuration>
                    <archive>
                        <manifest>
                            <mainClass>com.example.App</mainClass>
                        </manifest>
                    </archive>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <!-- Bundle the facade and its runtime binding into one runnable jar -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.6.0</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <phase>package</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>shade</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <transformers>
                                <transformer implementation="org.apache.maven.plugins.shade.resource.ManifestResourceTransformer">
                                    <mainClass>com.example.App</mainClass>
                                </transformer>
                                <transformer implementation="org.apache.maven.plugins.shade.resource.ServicesResourceTransformer"/>
                            </transformers>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>

Key points:
- `slf4j-api` (`pom.xml:31`) is the only logging dependency app code compiles against.
- `logback-classic` is `runtime` scope (`pom.xml:38`) — swap this single dependency to change backends (log4j2, JUL, etc.) without touching code.
- Classes use `LoggerFactory.getLogger(Class)`; config lives in `logback.xml`.
- `maven-shade-plugin` bundles facade + binding into a runnable jar: `mvn package && java -jar target/app-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar`.
